repositories.brief_summary: Configurable domain/thread stack sizes, Windows filename/`stat` hardening, and an ephemeron-termination fix landed on trunk this week.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=...'` stack-size option, Windows `Sys`/`Filename` fixes, and ephemeron GC correctness fixes merged to trunk.
repositories.new_features:
- New `OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=<bytes>'` option lets programs configure the minimum **system stack size** used when spawning a `Thread` or `Domain`, useful for FFI code that needs a larger native stack; documented in `man/ocamlrun.1`, the reference manual, `Thread.create` and `Domain.spawn` ([#14195](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14195), [#14860](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14860)) by [@Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse), reviewed by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA)
- `Sys.file_exists`/related `Sys` primitives now use `GetFileAttributes` instead of `stat_os` on Windows, avoiding a kernel bug in `GetFileInformationByName` that made `Sys.file_exists "C:\\...\\repro:xxx"` wrongly return `true` ([#14919](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14919), reported as [#14911](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14911)-adjacent in [#14919](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14919)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)
- `Filename` functions on Windows now treat `:` strictly as the drive/volume separator rather than sometimes as a directory separator, fixing surprising results from `Filename.concat` on paths like `C:\Foo:` ([#14871](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14871), [#14916](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14916)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)
- Fixed a hang in `caml_shutdown()` under `OCAMLRUNPARAM="c=1"` (cleanup-at-exit mode) where the final GC cycle could get stuck in `Phase_sweep_and_mark_main` because orphaned ephemerons from a terminated domain were never adopted ([#14906](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14906)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole)
- Multicore GC now waits for **all domains** to finish marking before starting another round of ephemeron marking, avoiding unnecessary marking work at the cost of potentially longer GC cycles in some workloads ([#14774](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14774)) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), reviewed by [Damien Doligez](https://github.com/damiendoligez)
- `Unix.EACCES` documentation typo fixed (previously misspelled `EACCESS`) in `unix.mli`/`unixLabels.mli` ([#14920](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14920)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- Memory-model documentation comments in `runtime/memory.c` clarified to be more precise about how GC frontiers update ([#14857](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14857), [#14924](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14924)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole)
- `HACKING.adoc` build documentation pinned to Ubuntu 24.04 for reproducible dev-environment setup ([#14926](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14926)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist)

repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered atomic-load bugs in record updates, a rejected pattern-matching sugar proposal, and Format indentation semantics.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) reported that functional record updates (`{ r with j }`) on records with `[@atomic]` fields silently emit implicit atomic loads without the same protection as pattern matching; [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) and [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) agreed this was an oversight that should be forbidden, while updates that fully overwrite all atomic fields (with no implicit load) should remain accepted ([#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918))
- [Christophe Raffalli](https://github.com/craff) proposed a `#x` pattern-matching syntax for constant patterns as sugar for a `when` clause; after triage-meeting discussion, [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) and [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) judged the syntactic translation brittle and a likely source of bugs, recommending explicit `when` clauses or a PPX instead; the issue was closed ([#14908](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14908))
- [Alain Frisch](https://github.com/alainfrisch) investigated counter-intuitive `Format` module wrapping behavior where a smaller indentation produced more line-wrapping than a larger one, and closed the issue after confirming it reflects documented (if surprising) behavior of the default structural box type distinct from `hov` boxes ([#14917](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14917))
- [Romain Beauxis](https://github.com/toots) and [Pierre-Yves Strub](https://github.com/strub) discussed GC pacing and default parameter regressions between OCaml 4.14 and 5.x, with `custom_major_ratio` tuning reported to resolve a 5x checking-time blow-up seen in EasyCrypt on 5.5, feeding into the GC-pacing rework tracked in [#14796](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14796) ([#14533](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14533))

repositories.brief_summary: Opam 2.5.2 shipped alongside a CVE-2026-57825 symlink fix and a repository-archive storage change that speeds up update/init.
repositories.new_features_summary: Repository archive storage speeds up update/init; CVE-2026-57825 symlink fix and .install path/root-section fixes shipped in 2.5.2.
repositories.new_features:
- Internal opam-root **repository storage** switched from plain directories to gzipped tar archives for HTTP repositories (and any non-VCS repository when `OPAMREPOSITORYTARRING` is set), improving update/init performance on NTFS and IO-constrained machines, with a conditional opam-root upgrade to format **2.6** triggered automatically ([#6625](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6625) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate), [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou), [@arozovyk](https://github.com/arozovyk) — fixes [#5346](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5346), [#5741](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5741), [#5648](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5648), [#5484](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5484), [#5559](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5559), [#3050](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/3050), [#6974](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6974))
- Fixed a **symlink bypass** of the switch prefix check during install, tracked as **CVE-2026-57825**, and backported to the 2.5 branch ([#7005](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7005), [#7006](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7006) by [Nathan Rebours](https://github.com/NathanReb) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- `.install` files containing `..` in destination paths are **re-allowed** (after being invalidated in [#6897](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6897)) while no longer creating unnecessary intermediate directories, and gained new `root` / `rootexec` sections ([#7008](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7008), [#7015](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7015) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate); [#6938](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6938) by [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian))
- Fixed `opam pin add <url-to-archive>` failing to extract the archive before building, so pinning a bare archive URL now works the same as `opam pin add <pkg> <archive>` ([#7012](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7012) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) — fixes [#6999](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6999))
- Fixed `OpamFilename.starts_with` and `dir_starts_with` incorrectly treating `foo/bar` as a prefix of `foo/bar-baz`, and made `/` and `\` equivalent on Windows, backported to 2.5 ([#6953](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6953), [#7003](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7003) by [Nathan Rebours](https://github.com/NathanReb) — fixes [#6948](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6948))
- Fixed `OpamSystem.real_path` failing to resolve `..` segments occurring after a non-existent path component, backported to 2.5 ([#7011](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7011), [#7013](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7013) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) — fixes [#7010](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7010))
- Darcs VCS backend no longer falls back to "Num Patches" when computing weak hashes, since "Weak Hash" support has been available since 2016 ([#6866](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6866) by [@toastal](https://github.com/toastal))
- Fixed the Cygwin CI build by pinning `gcc` to 13.4 (14.4 breaks C++ support), and upgraded CI coverage to **OCaml 5.5** and **4.14.4** ([#7007](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7007), [#6988](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6988) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Released **opam 2.5.2** and added it to the install scripts ([#7016](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7016), [#7017](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7017), [#7018](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7018) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs target filename-prefix consistency and clearer error messages, while a Windows `.install` test suite surfaced follow-up bugs.
repositories.activity:
- Two **new PRs opened** this week remain unmerged: a consistency fix so `OpamFilename.remove_prefix` matches the corrected `starts_with` semantics, by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([#7004](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7004)), and a clearer error message for `opam repo add`/`set-url` when a repository name is already globally registered, by [@yannl35133](https://github.com/yannl35133) addressing their own report ([#7014](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7014), fixes [#6943](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6943))
- An exhaustive **`.install` field reftest suite** covering Windows and Unix paths was merged ([#6956](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6956) by [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou)), and reviewing it surfaced three Windows-specific bugs filed as follow-ups: files without a `.install`-added `.exe` suffix not being cleaned up on removal ([#7021](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7021)), binaries installed via the `libexec` field failing ([#7022](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7022)), and inconsistent path display across platforms in tests and user output ([#7023](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7023))
- Follow-up issues were opened to track remaining test coverage gaps from the repository-archive work, including exercising `OPAMREPOSITORYTARRING` across the whole reftest suite ([#7024](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7024)) and adding more Windows `.install` tests ([#7025](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7025)), plus a request for Mercurial/Darcs test coverage referencing the Darcs weak-hash fix ([#7019](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7019) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Longer-running **performance and UX proposals** stayed open from prior weeks, including multicore parallelism for `opam install` plan presentation reporting a 40% speed-up ([#5877](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5877) by [Michael Bacarella](https://github.com/mbacarella)), switching the default solver from `builtin-mccs+glpk` to `builtin-0install` ([#6586](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6586)), speeding up `opam update` when nothing changed ([#6283](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6283)), and speeding up local git pinning by avoiding the git transport protocol ([#6838](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6838)), all by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- Other **ongoing open PRs** include basic tracing support ([#5757](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5757) by [Simon Cruanes](https://github.com/c-cube)), package spelling hints ([#6434](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6434) by [@arozovyk](https://github.com/arozovyk)), an `env` flag to print environment-variable bindings ([#6316](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6316) by [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou)), and homogenizing initial vs. diff-based repository loads ([#6924](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6924) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Issues closed this week following the repository-archive and path-resolution fixes include repeated reports of slow `opam update` and large downloads on Windows/macOS ([#3050](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/3050), [#5484](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5484), [#5559](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5559), [#5648](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5648), [#5741](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/5741), [#6974](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6974)), the `starts_with` bug ([#6948](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6948)), and the `real_path` resolution bug ([#7010](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7010))

repositories.trends_summary: Windows-specific `.install` edge cases and OCaml 5.5 platform support are driving new issues and CI work.
repositories.emerging_trends:

repositories.brief_summary: Ppx hover expansion rewritten to use Merlin directly, and a batch of Stdune module removals landed alongside an OCaml 5.5 sandbox switch.
repositories.new_features_summary: Hover on ppx-derived code now delegates to Merlin's expand-ppx command, fixing broken expansions, and the nix sandbox defaults to OCaml 5.5.
repositories.new_features:
- Reworked **ppx hover expansion** to call Merlin's `expand-ppx` command directly instead of hand-reconstructing the expected output, fixing broken hover text for `[@@deriving ...]` on mutually recursive types by [PixieDust](https://github.com/PizieDust) ([#1615](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1615), fixes [#1614](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1614)), removing roughly 110 lines of duplicated expansion-reconstruction logic from `hover_req.ml`
- Switched the nix development sandbox's default OCaml version to **5.5** by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#1616](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1616)), tracking the OCaml 5.5 support request in [#1596](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1596)
- Corrected the JSON response schema example in the `ocamllsp/typeSearch` documentation, which had incorrectly nested an array inside an object instead of an array of result objects, by [Clément Delafargue](https://github.com/divarvel) ([#1613](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1613))
repositories.activity_summary: Rudi Grinberg opened a batch of Stdune cleanup PRs and merged several; dependabot bumps and a Dune-formatting scope fix remained open at week's end.
repositories.activity:
- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) opened a batch of **Stdune module removal** PRs that had not merged by week's end, including dropping `Stdune.Map` ([#1620](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1620)), removing a leftover polymorphic compare ([#1617](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1617)), switching the LSP metamodel generator to the `top-closure` package ([#1630](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1630)), further **stdune cruft** removal ([#1632](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1632)), removing unused libraries ([#1633](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1633)), and an attempt to remove `Stdune.Io` that was closed unmerged after conflicts ([#1628](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1628))
- Five automated **dependency bump** PRs from dependabot remained open at week's end, covering `picomatch` ([#1623](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1623)), `minimatch` ([#1624](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1624)), `js-yaml` ([#1625](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1625)), `brace-expansion` ([#1626](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1626)), and `@babel/core` ([#1627](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1627))
- [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) opened a fix **restricting Dune S-expression formatting** to actual Dune documents by introducing an abstract `Document.Dune.t` type, preventing OCamllex, Menhir and Cram documents from being misrouted through Dune's formatter ([#1621](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1621), related to ocamllabs/vscode-ocaml-platform#1159 and ocamllabs/vscode-ocaml-platform#1487), which merged just after the review window closed
- Continuing the **Stdune cleanup**, [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) merged removal of `Stdune.Int` ([#1619](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1619)) and `Stdune.Pid` ([#1631](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1631), which also made `Diagnostics.Dune.t` track a typed `Pid.t` instead of a bare `int`), and replaced copy-pasted file IO with the extracted `fs-io` package ([#1629](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1629))
- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) also merged an upgrade to **ocamlformat 0.28.1** in the nix environment ([#1618](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1618)), and dependabot's bumps of `cachix/install-nix-action` ([#1504](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1504)) and `@types/node` ([#1510](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1510)) merged
- The **hover-on-warnings** PR remains open pending design discussion, with [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) noting the added warning-detail-on-hover behavior goes beyond the scope of the originating issue and needs further design discussion before merging ([#1606](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1606), tracking [#717](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/717))
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered an opam solver downgrade problem, a proposed ocamlgrep integration, and a workspace/symbol performance report.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#1604](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1604), [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) reported that `opam upgrade` attempts to downgrade `ocaml-lsp-server` from `1.21.0-4.14` to `1.17.0` on OCaml 4.14; [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) explained there is no clean fix in the package itself and suggested pinning the package or switching to the `builtin-0install` solver, citing a similar prior report at ocaml/opam#6951
- On [#1607](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1607), [Martin Jambon](https://github.com/mjambon) proposed integrating **ocamlgrep**, a structural search tool that scans `.cmt` files with typed OCaml expression patterns, directly into `ocaml-lsp` rather than through Merlin, sharing a VS Code demo and a draft integration PR (mjambon#2) done for LexiFi under [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb)'s supervision
- On [#1622](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1622), [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) documented that `workspace/symbol` took over 13 seconds and returned an empty result in a roughly 50,000-file monorepo, tracing the latency to a full recursive re-scan and re-parse of every `.cmt`/`.cmti` file on each request with no retained symbol index, cross-referencing the original report at ocamllabs/vscode-ocaml-platform#1156
- On [#1615](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1615), [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) pushed [PixieDust](https://github.com/PizieDust) to simplify the ppx-hover patch by collapsing two redundant attribute-matching variants into one, after clarifying that the hover popup should trigger anywhere within the `deriving` attribute rather than only on the attribute name
repositories.trends_summary: Rudi Grinberg's Stdune-reduction push and a fresh large-workspace performance report both point toward simplifying and scaling the server's internals.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- A sustained effort by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) to shrink and remove the internal `Stdune` compatibility layer in favor of small standalone packages, replacing `Stdune.Int`, `Stdune.Map`, `Stdune.Pid`, and `Stdune.Io` with dedicated libraries such as `fs-io` and `top-closure` ([#1617](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1617), [#1619](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1619), [#1620](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1620), [#1629](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1629), [#1630](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1630), [#1631](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1631), [#1632](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1632), [#1633](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1633))
- Growing attention to **performance at scale** in large monorepos, seen in the new `workspace/symbol` latency report ([#1622](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1622)) following closely on the OCaml 5.5 compatibility push ([#1596](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1596), [#1616](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1616))
- A preference for **delegating to Merlin** rather than reimplementing logic in `ocaml-lsp` itself, illustrated both by the ppx-hover rewrite to call Merlin's `expand-ppx` directly ([#1615](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1615)) and by the proposed ocamlgrep integration built on `compiler-libs` outside of Merlin ([#1607](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1607))

repositories.brief_summary: Dune fixed OCaml 5.5 compatibility regressions, hardened install/process-spawn handling, and began the 3.24.1 patch release.
repositories.new_features_summary: Fixes for OCaml 5.5 relocatable-compiler detection, C compiler vendor recognition, config-file crashes, and install logging.
repositories.new_features:
- `compilation_mode`: exposed the internal `repr` accessor so downstream libraries using Dune's OCaml libraries can pattern-match on compilation mode ([#15487](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15487)) by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro).
- Fixed **relocatable compiler detection** for OCaml >= 5.5, replacing a heuristic that stopped firing correctly on vanilla 5.5.0 with a version check ([#15444](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15444), fixes [#15443](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15443)) by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter).
- **C compiler vendor detection** now aligns with the OCaml compiler's own identifiers (`msvc`, `icc`, `mingw`, `clang`, `gcc`, `xlc`, `sunc`), fixing a spurious warning for compilers dune previously failed to recognize ([#15423](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15423), fixes [#14870](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14870)) by [Chizy](https://github.com/chizy7).
- Fixed an internal error (`modules_and_obj_dir: failed lookup`) when generating `js_of_ocaml` archive rules for a `dune` file defining two libraries with the same name distinguished by mutually exclusive `enabled_if` clauses, as `ocaml-re` does ([#14904](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14904), fixes [#14775](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14775)) by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon).
- Dune no longer crashes when `~/.config/dune` is a regular file instead of a directory, treating `ENOTDIR` as "path does not exist" ([#15475](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15475), fixes [#15406](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15406)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Installed `dune-package` files now emit **relative artifact references** even when an absolute external `DUNE_BUILD_DIR` is used, avoiding build-directory-dependent archive and module paths ([#15077](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15077), fixes [#11774](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/11774)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- `dune install` now validates or creates the destination directory **before** printing the "Installing ..." line, avoiding misleading log output when an intermediate path turns out to be a file ([#15480](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15480)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Dropped the `lsof`-based fallback for counting open file descriptors, since spawning `lsof` isn't allowed outside the scheduler's process reaping ([#15477](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15477)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- On Linux, dune now waits for a spawned **process group** to fully exit after its leader dies, tightening what counts as a successfully completed action ([#14868](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14868)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Added a new **shell completion** documentation page covering Bash, Zsh, and PowerShell setup for `dune completion` ([#15403](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15403), commit [cf9bac6](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/commit/cf9bac60724b7d56bea3273f276793f0833569e7)) by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV).
- Clarified that `dune runtest`/`dune test` are **not exactly equivalent** to `dune build @runtest` in workspaces with multiple build contexts, documenting context-selection behavior ([#15449](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15449), fixes [#15405](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15405)) by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter).
repositories.activity_summary: The 3.24.1 patch release moved forward with backports, alongside an internal refactor of stdune's process-spawning code and new `describe` work.
repositories.activity:

repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered a Bazel remote-execution proposal, `dune exec` binary resolution semantics, and root causes of two 3.24.0 regressions.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) opened a design discussion on supporting **Bazel's Remote Execution API** so dune could use distributed-build services like BuildBuddy or Buildbarn, noting incompatibility with the current DAP-based action runner and sketching a possible approach ([#15472](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15472)).
- [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter), and [Gaëtan Gilbert](https://github.com/SkySkimmer) discussed why `dune exec -- prog` now resolves binaries under `_build/default` instead of `_build/install/default/bin`, tracing it to the intentional `%{bin:...}` semantics change in a previous release and identifying a missing dune-lang-version guard on `%{pkg:...}` as a related gap ([#15458](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15458)).
- [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter), and [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) traced spurious compiler rebuilds under package management with the cache disabled to `ocamlfind`'s `topfind` helper invalidating the compiler's install target, fixed upstream via an opam-overlay change rather than in dune itself ([#15409](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15409)).
- [Greg Troxel](https://github.com/gdt) and [@0-wiz-0](https://github.com/0-wiz-0) diagnosed a 3.24.0 regression breaking `lablgtk3` builds, resolved by patches from an upstream `lablgtk` pull request rather than a dune change ([#15429](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15429)).

repositories.brief_summary: cmx-file installation landed, an ld.conf path fix was proposed, and nine long-standing issues were closed
repositories.new_features_summary: cmx files now installed to prevent warning 58, CI workflow expanded with more test coverage, thread-package lookup exception fixed
repositories.new_features:
- Findlib now installs `.cmx` files alongside `.cmi` files during `make install`, resolving `no-cmx-file` (**warning 58**) reports in client projects such as Rocq ([#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/120), fixes [#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117)) by [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai).
- Fixed the **`threads` package lookup** to catch `No_such_package` instead of the outdated `Not_found` exception, restoring `ocamlfind ocamlopt -config` on compilers built with `--disable-systhreads` ([#99](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/99)) by [@shym](https://github.com/shym).
- **CI workflow** updated to `actions/checkout@v6`, given named steps for readability, and extended to exercise `ocamlfind printconf` and `ocamlfind opt` alongside the existing `ocamlfind list` and toplevel-plugin checks ([#116](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/116)) by [@shym](https://github.com/shym).
- Added `ocamlfind_opt` to `.gitignore` following the CI update ([a58e7cc](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/commit/a58e7ccab9820377a7fdbd459ea5e57281da97f1)).
repositories.activity_summary: New PR proposes making ld.conf paths absolute for OCaml 5.5.0 support; maintainer closed nine long-standing issues
repositories.activity:
- [Rodolphe Lepigre](https://github.com/rlepigre-skylabs-ai) opened [#119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/119), proposing to make relative paths read from **`ld.conf`** absolute so that the `stublibs` entries shipped in OCaml 5.5.0's `ld.conf` resolve correctly; the author notes the resulting paths aren't normalized and flags open questions about the install/uninstall codepath.
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) closed nine long-standing **issue-triage** items spanning packaging and installation problems, including a Cygwin/opam build failure ([#84](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/84)), a Gentoo linker error ([#24](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/24)), a Coq Platform patch-file error ([#96](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/96)), an unreachable `camlcity.org` source tarball ([#108](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/108), [#98](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/98)), an `ocaml 4.00.1` build failure ([#58](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/58)), a Windows carriage-return output problem ([#70](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/70)), and older requests around `num` handling and CMI exports ([#1](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/1), [#7](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/7)).
- Merged fixes landed for the **`threads` package detection** regression ([#99](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/99)) and **cmx-file installation** ([#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/120)), alongside the CI overhaul ([#116](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/116)).
- [Kabir G](https://github.com/kabirbg) reported difficulty getting `ocamlfind` (installed via Fedora's `dnf`) to see a `camlidl` package installed to `/usr/lib64/ocaml` ([#118](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/118)); the issue remains **open** pending investigation of the Fedora package's missing `META` file.
repositories.discussions_summary: Troubleshooting a missing META file for Fedora's dnf-packaged camlidl narrowed the cause to the distro package rather than ocamlfind
repositories.notable_discussions:
- In [#118](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/118), [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) walked [Kabir G](https://github.com/kabirbg) through `ocamlfind printconf` and search-path inspection, narrowing a "package not found" report on Fedora down to the `dnf`-packaged `camlidl` missing its `META` file — pointing at a **Fedora packaging gap** rather than an ocamlfind bug.
- In [#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117), [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) weighed installing `.cmx` files against having `configure` detect `-opaque` compiler support, concluding installing `.cmx` files was the simpler fix — implemented in [#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/pull/120).

repositories.brief_summary: Legacy OCaml <4.08 compatibility code removed from the loader and model, plus continued work on OxCaml modes and include functor support.
repositories.new_features_summary: Loader and model cleanup dropping OCaml <4.08 compatibility branches, and an opam version constraint fix.
repositories.new_features:
- Removed dead compatibility code paths for OCaml versions older than 4.08 across `cmi.ml`/`cmi.mli`, `cmt.ml`, `cmti.ml`, `doc_attr.ml`, `ident_env.ml`, `compat.cppo.ml`, and `syntax_highlighter.ml`, simplifying conditional cppo branches such as the `read_label` signature in the loader by [Corentin De Souza](https://github.com/fantazio) ([#1458](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1458))

- Eliminated a duplicate branch in the module-loading code discovered while investigating `include functor` support, with both sides of the branch verified identical by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([#1460](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1460))
repositories.activity_summary: Ongoing PRs cover OxCaml mode rendering and include-functor support, alongside a voodoo-mode transitive dependency fix that was closed unmerged.
repositories.activity:
- [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) continues work on rendering OxCaml **modes** in generated documentation, including heuristics to omit modes that are legacy, implied by other axes, or inferable from context on arrow types, with review feedback on record-type refactoring and mode-flip edge cases from [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) and [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454))
- [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) is extending `include functor` support for OxCaml so included items show they originated via the functor, with [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) identifying missing logic for cases where the functor body references the including module's own types (illustrated with a `module F`/`module M` reproduction) and suggesting a dummy-module preprocessing approach ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452))
- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) opened and then closed a driver fix for **voodoo mode** that recorded module hashes in per-library stamp files to resolve transitive (not just direct) dependencies from META files, commenting he had "a better idea" ([#1457](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1457))
- The OCaml **<4.08 removal** effort traces back to an earlier merged PR by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1300](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1300)), completed this week in the loader/model code by [Corentin De Souza](https://github.com/fantazio), with [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) reviewing and applying a "no changelog" label since compatibility was already dropped in 3.1.0 ([#1458](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1458), [#1300](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1300))
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion on resolving name collisions between sibling libraries with matching module names in odoc_driver's link/compile ordering.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) raised how `odoc_driver` resolves same-named modules across sibling libraries (Eliom's `eliom.client` and `eliom.server`, which intentionally share module names for client/server symmetry), where client documentation was resolving to server definitions ([#1450](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1450))
- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) responded that current `odoc_driver` behavior is wrong and proposed separating `odoc compile` (using only a module's actual compile-time dependencies from `compile-deps`) from `odoc link` (using the union of all package/library dependencies, disambiguated via explicit `{!/library_name/Module}` references), committing to open a PR ([#1450](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1450))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued cleanup of legacy code paths alongside OxCaml-related feature work (modes, include functor) surfacing edge cases in type and jkind handling.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Removal of legacy compatibility code (OCaml <4.08) is reducing branching complexity in the loader, as noted when eliminating a leftover duplicate branch during `include functor` investigation ([#1458](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1458), [#1460](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1460))
- OxCaml-specific features (modes rendering, `include functor`) are surfacing deeper resolution issues in type expression and jkind-annotation handling, echoed by a separate report of a `Failure("invalid core type")` exception while reading jkind annotations when building `base`'s docs with oxcaml ([#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454), [#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452), [#1455](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1455))
- Cross-library and cross-package reference resolution remains a recurring pain point, spanning both the sibling-library name collision in `odoc_driver` and a separate false-positive "hidden constructors" warning for re-exported wrapped-library types generated by Menhir's `--table` incremental API ([#1450](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1450), [#1459](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1459))
repositories.contributors_summary: Contributions this week spanned OxCaml feature work, legacy code removal, driver debugging, and issue triage/discussion on cross-library resolution.
repositories.contributors:

repositories.brief_summary: WebGL2 bindings and a messageEvent type consolidation merged, plus a cluster of compiler correctness fixes and CI restructuring.
repositories.new_features_summary: WebGL2 bindings, unified messageEvent type, js_simpl/js_traverse miscompilation fixes, and Windows wasm-toplevel/OCaml 5.6 support merged.
repositories.new_features:
- WebGL2 bindings via a new `WebGL2` module inheriting `WebGL`'s rendering context, adding 3D/immutable textures, multiple render targets, instanced drawing, uniform buffer objects, transform feedback, and a new `webgl2_particles` example, closing a long-standing request from [Christophe Raffalli](https://github.com/craff) ([#2388](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2388), [#1226](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1226))
- Consolidated five duplicate `messageEvent` class types (`Worker`, `WebSockets`, `EventSource`, `MessageChannel`, `Dom_html`) into a single polymorphic `Dom_html.messageEvent`, keeping the old per-module types as deprecated aliases for source compatibility ([#2390](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2390), [#2382](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2382))
- Fixed a **miscompilation** in `js_simpl`'s `if`-fusion that could collapse two evaluations of an effectful expression into a single call, plus related bugs dropping hoisted `var` declarations from folded constant `if` branches and missing variable uses in catch-parameter destructuring defaults ([#2393](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2393), [#2285](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2285))
- Fixed **wasm toplevels built on Windows**: embedded cmi paths used backslash separators that the virtual filesystem's lookups did not normalize, causing `Env.Error` on OCaml >= 5.4 ([#2397](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2397))
- `wasm_of_ocaml --toplevel` now embeds cmis (Stdlib, compiler-libs, ...) when building with **separate compilation**, not just whole-program compilation, so separately-compiled wasm toplevels can load Stdlib at startup ([#1721](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1721))
- Fixed polymorphic comparison between an **immediate value and a custom block** that provides a `compare_ext` operation (e.g. zarith), restoring correctness broken by an earlier change ([#2391](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2391))
- Merged **initial support for OCaml 5.6**, covering effect continuations, primitive descriptions, toplevel error formatting and runtime hash-table primitives ([#2227](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2227), [#2142](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2142))
- Updated the **manual sidebar ordering** with `@children_order` so odoc follows the logical reading order, and removed obsolete redirect-stub manual pages left over from the wiki conversion, by [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) ([#2359](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2359))
repositories.activity_summary: Three unmerged PRs opened for ESM output, Web Audio/Media Capture and BroadcastChannel/SharedWorker bindings, alongside a CI restructuring cluster.
repositories.activity:
- Three **new PRs opened** this week remain under review: an experimental ES module output mode (`--esm`) framed as an RFC to inform the ESM design discussion ([#2402](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2402)), bindings for the **Web Audio and Media Capture APIs** completing the `Dom_html.mediaElement` binding ([#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401)), and bindings for **BroadcastChannel and SharedWorker** filling the remaining Tier 2 communication gaps ([#2400](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2400)), all opened by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo).
- CI infrastructure saw a cluster of merged cleanups by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo): deduping the Jane Street test suite into a dedicated workflow ([#2394](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2394)), moving build-only compiler coverage out of the main test matrix ([#2396](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2396)), aligning tool workflows on OCaml 5.5 and folding the Wax check into lint ([#2395](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2395)), and sharing the `ci_setup` script between the mainstream and OxCaml variants via `Re` ([#2398](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2398)).
- The **experimental ESM tooling** branch ([#2163](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2163)) gained four bug fixes this week — correcting module evaluation order, external-import resolution, and tree-shaking of entry-point side effects and namespace imports — found while building the `--esm` RFC on top of it ([#2402](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2402)).
- [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) continued work on draft optimization and portability PRs: converting runtime files to use Wax ([#2373](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2373)), resolving wasm assets relative to the runtime file instead of `require.main` ([#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2389)), and extracting toplevel loops into helper closures to help engines tier up initialization code ([#2245](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2245)).
- [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole)'s lambda-lifting performance work remains in draft, including more aggressive lifting measured at a 1.45x speedup on a Bonsai benchmark ([#1886](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1886)) and only lifting functions with free variables ([#1885](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1885)).
- [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) closed two experimental compiler PRs without merging — preserving block sharing ([#2184](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2184)) and speeding up substitution ([#2185](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2185)) — alongside ongoing drafts for inlining runtime-defined primitives into generated code ([#1928](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1928)) and physical-equality hints ([#1745](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1745)).
- [Jason Gross](https://github.com/JasonGross) continued a community-contributed PR dispatching lifecycle events (`wasmoocaml:loaded`/`wasmoocaml:error`) when async Wasm instantiation completes, ported from the former `ocaml-wasm/wasm_of_ocaml` repository ([#2232](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2232)).
repositories.discussions_summary: The Temporal-polyfill code-size report and the messageEvent/ESM design threads were the main technical discussions this week.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- A large **Temporal polyfill** (~12k lines) unexpectedly appearing in compiled JS for a 6.4 user was traced by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) and [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian), not to js_of_ocaml itself but to a dead-code-elimination gap combined with an unconditionally-included JavaScript file in a bumped janestreet/core dependency, connecting back to [stan-dev/stanc3#1631](https://github.com/stan-dev/stanc3/pull/1631) and [stan-dev/stanc3#1640](https://github.com/stan-dev/stanc3/issues/1640) ([#2399](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2399)).
- Discussion on [#2382](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2382) about consolidating the duplicate `messageEvent` types weighed a two-type-parameter design (target and data) against keeping historical per-module aliases for source compatibility, ultimately implemented in [#2390](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2390).
- The **ESM RFC** ([#2402](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2402)) frames a design question for separate compilation — bundled vs. unbundled module output — with measured size and link-time tradeoffs, feeding into the longer-running discussions in [#1161](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1161) and [#551](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/551).

repositories.brief_summary: Reaper unboxing extended to boxed numbers, atomic-field safety checks landed, and x86 peephole fixes shipped alongside jkind precision work.
repositories.new_features_summary: Reaper unboxing extended to boxed numbers, atomic-field safety checks, x86 peephole fixes, and a new imprecise-kind-annotation warning.
repositories.new_features:
- Reworked how fibers store dynamic bindings: each fiber now keeps a growable stack table (replacing the hash-table code removed earlier), with new `caml_dynamic_push`/`caml_dynamic_pop` primitives so `with_temporarily` no longer needs a fresh fiber, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([5b3304c](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/commit/5b3304cf5497ad098193e979c04d59f6342fe977))
- Functional record updates (`{ t with x = 42 }`) that would implicitly perform a nonatomic read of an `[@atomic]` field are now rejected during typechecking, closing upstream ocaml/ocaml#14918, by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([#6453](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6453))
- Mode **coercion** on function return values is now allowed for non-local axes, e.g. `int -> int :> int -> int @ portable`, by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([#6407](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6407))
- Correctness fixes for the `-x86-peephole-optimize` pass (stale-address `mov` elision, BSF/BSR destination tracking, flag-preserving `addq $n, %rsp` merging) plus a restructuring of `X86_proc` so peephole rewrites now also reach the internal-assembler output, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6426](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6426))
- Reaper's unboxing transformation extended to boxed `int32`/`int64`/`nativeint` numbers via a new `Boxed_number` field constructor, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6437](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6437))
- New `imprecise-kind-annotation` warning (191) flags kind annotations on type/value declarations that differ from the inferred jkind, by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([#5362](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5362))
- First-class modules are now supported inside quotes, with automatic annotation insertion for packing/unpacking expressions, by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) ([#5884](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5884))
- Fixed the dynamic-binding cache not being flushed around callbacks from C, which could leave a stale fiber's bindings visible, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6380](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6380))
- Fixed `module rec` type approximation over-widening abstract types with `with`-bound kind annotations to layout `any`, causing spurious errors, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6395](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6395))
- Merlin gains keyword-edition handling (cherry-picked from upstream), letting the internal build default to the pre-`effect` (5.2) keyword set, by [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) ([#6442](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6442))
- Reaper improvements: production of the new poison value in terms, and new counters tracking unboxing activity, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6314](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6314), [#6409](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6409))
- The `simplify` pass now prevents variant unboxing when the unboxed fields are unavailable at all use sites, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6282](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6282))
- Fixed kind path substitution in `Tof_kind`, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6401](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6401))
- Reaper design documentation added to the Flambda2 encyclopaedia, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6419](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6419))

repositories.trends_summary: Sustained reaper and jkind/ikind precision investment, plus growing atomic-field safety checks and internal tooling.

repositories.brief_summary: Eio.Net.getaddrinfo now raises detailed errors instead of returning empty lists, and Eio.Path.load was fixed for zero-size /proc files.
repositories.new_features_summary: Getaddrinfo error reporting, `/proc`-safe `Path.load`, `chown`/`chmod` symlink hardening, and `File.Stat` disk-usage fields landed.
repositories.new_features:
- `Eio.Net.getaddrinfo`, `getaddrinfo_stream` and `getaddrinfo_datagram` no longer silently return `[]` on failure; they now raise `Eio.Io (Eio.Net.E (Address_lookup_failed _), _)` carrying a new `Getaddrinfo_error.t` error code (mirroring `gai_strerror(3)`), fixing a case where the actual DNS/socket-resolution failure was previously invisible to callers, implemented by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) building on earlier work by [Christiano Haesbaert](https://github.com/haesbaert) ([#866](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/866), fixes [#776](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/776) and [#351](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/351))
- `Eio.Path.load` reworked to use a buffered reader with a sensible minimum initial size instead of pre-allocating a buffer from `stat`, fixing failures reading zero-size files such as those under `/proc` by [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#869](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/869), [#878](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/878), fixes [#798](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/798) and [#835](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/835))
- `Eio.File.Stat.t` gains `blksize` and `blocks` fields for computing on-disk usage, with `fstat` switched to `statx` on Linux (requiring Linux 5.18+ when using the uring backend for stat) by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#865](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/865))
- `Eio.Path.chown` hardened against sandbox escape via symlinks, resolving the target with `O_PATH`/`AT_EMPTY_PATH` on `eio_linux` and re-checking on `eio_posix` by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#877](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/877))
- `chmod` similarly hardened against sandbox escape via symlinks, always using no-follow at the syscall level for confined paths by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#872](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/872))
- Fixed a file-descriptor lifetime bug in `eio_linux` low-level read/write functions that did not hold the fd open before entering the scheduler, unlike the readv/writev equivalents, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#871](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/871))
- `eio_linux` switched to the `Uring.Res` module for safer, more explicit error handling in `connect`, `noop`, `statx` and `unlink` by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#868](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/868))
- `eio_posix` and `eio_windows` now map `ENOPROTOOPT` to `Eio.Net.Invalid_option` for consistency with `eio_linux` by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#874](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/874))
- `fork_action` now retries on `EINTR` when writing to its error pipe by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#870](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/870))
- Socket-option string handling made more robust against unterminated strings, with documentation on why it is tricky, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#876](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/876))
- Windows build fixed by declaring `unixsupport` functions `CAMLextern`, preventing flexdll `RELOC_REL32` errors when dynamically loading and unblocking mdx tests, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) with the fix suggested by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#881](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/881))
- macOS compiler warnings silenced by adding braces around a switch-case block by [Olaf Hering](https://github.com/olafhering) ([#882](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/882))
- Minimum `uring` dependency bumped to 2.15.0+ to use its new functionality, with CI/bench Dockerfiles moved to OCaml 5.5, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#867](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/867))
- Removed the unused `show_backend_exceptions` flag, since `Backend.show` is the one actually exposed in the public API, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#880](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/880))
- README wording clarified so Eio is described as implementing functionality similar to **Lwt** or **Async** via effects, rather than claiming to replace them outright, by [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) following discussion with [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [@redianthus](https://github.com/redianthus) ([#879](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/879))
repositories.activity_summary: An open PR proposes a pre-connect socket-options DSL, while sandbox and getaddrinfo fixes closed several long-standing issues.
repositories.activity:
- A **pre-connect socket options** PR remains open, exposing a GADT-based DSL for specifying bind/setsockopt behaviour before connecting, opened by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) building on earlier work by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w), with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) raising concerns that the DSL is turning into a "little language" and suggesting a lower-level BSD-sockets-style API alongside it ([#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875), follow-up to [#713](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/713))
- A **getsockopt_string truncation-check** PR was closed without merging after [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) concluded through discussion that the original bounds check was already correct ([#873](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/873))
- [Christiano Haesbaert](https://github.com/haesbaert)'s older PR proposing to return an empty list on `EAI_*` errors from `getaddrinfo` was closed as superseded, since [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) reimplemented the fix with fresh C stubs in [#866](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/866) ([#352](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/352))
- Several long-standing issues were closed this week as a result of the `getaddrinfo` error-reporting work and the eio_posix backend clean-up, including the original **getaddrinfo error propagation** report from [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) ([#351](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/351)), the **1019-connection resolution failure** reported by [Krzysztof Leśniak](https://github.com/serpent7776) ([#776](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/776)), and the umbrella **"Finish eio_posix backend"** tracking issue from [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#456](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/456))
- The `Eio.Path.load` race-condition reports from [Volker Diels-Grabsch](https://github.com/vog) and [@copy](https://github.com/copy) describing failures reading `/proc` files were both closed once the buffered-reader fix landed ([#835](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/835), [#798](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/798))
- [Marijan Petričević](https://github.com/marijanp) reported high iowait/IO-pressure readings for an idle io_uring-backed service, and after debugging with a bpftrace script [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) determined this reflects io_uring's own iowait accounting for reads from stdin rather than an Eio bug ([#862](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/862))
repositories.discussions_summary: Debate over whether socket connection options should be a DSL or a lower-level BSD-sockets API, plus README repositioning versus Lwt/Async.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On the pre-connect socket options PR, [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) questioned whether the growing options DSL is the right shape and suggested exposing a lower-level `setsockopt`/`bind_socket`/`connect_socket` API resembling BSD sockets; [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) responded that Eio's DSLs (including `Fork_action`) exist specifically so backends can interpret portable intent rather than raw calls, citing performance (parallel accept across domains), portability (an in-progress mirage-eio from [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht)), and tracing/backpressure as motivations ([#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875))
- The README's framing of Eio versus Lwt/Async was debated after [@redianthus](https://github.com/redianthus) argued that saying Eio "replaces" existing concurrency libraries overstates adoption reality, citing Ocsigen's decision to stay on Lwt; the discussion with [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) converged on describing Eio as implementing similar functionality via effects, with a note on interop difficulties across effect-using libraries ([#879](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/879))
- The `chmod`/`chown` sandbox-escape fixes prompted a detailed thread on kernel/glibc behaviour of `fchmodat2`, `AT_EMPTY_PATH` and `ENOSYS` fallbacks across Linux kernel versions between [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), including strace evidence from a 6.1 kernel VM ([#872](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/872))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued hardening of filesystem sandbox confinement and eio_linux error handling, alongside dependency/toolchain modernization.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **Sandbox-escape hardening** continues as a theme, following `chown` with `chmod` fixes for symlink handling this week, both flagged as related to a possible move to a modern glibc/kernel minimum ([#877](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/877), [#872](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/872), [#845](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/845))

- Design conversations increasingly reference a broader **portable-DSL philosophy** for Eio's frontend (sockets, filesystem, fork actions), weighing it against exposing lower-level backend-specific APIs ([#875](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/875))

group_summaries.brief_summary: Opam 2.5.2 fixed CVE-2026-57825 while OCaml 5.5 compatibility work continued across dune, ocamlfind, opam, and ocaml-lsp.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: Opam 2.5.2 shipped a symlink CVE fix, ocamlfind now installs cmx files, js_of_ocaml gained WebGL2, and ocaml-lsp's ppx hover now uses Merlin.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **[ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam)** released **opam 2.5.2**, fixing a symlink bypass of the switch-prefix check tracked as **CVE-2026-57825** ([ocaml/opam#7005](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7005), backported in [ocaml/opam#7006](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7006)), and switched internal repository storage from plain directories to gzipped tar archives to speed up `update`/`init` on NTFS and IO-constrained machines ([ocaml/opam#6625](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6625))
- **[ocaml/ocamlfind](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind)** now installs `.cmx` files alongside `.cmi` files during `make install`, resolving warning-58 reports in downstream projects such as Rocq ([ocaml/ocamlfind#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120), fixes [ocaml/ocamlfind#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117)), and fixed `threads` package lookup to catch the correct exception, restoring `ocamlfind ocamlopt -config` on compilers built without systhreads ([ocaml/ocamlfind#99](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/99))
- **[ocsigen/js_of_ocaml](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)** merged **WebGL2** bindings closing a long-standing request ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2388](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2388), [ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#1226](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1226)), consolidated five duplicate `messageEvent` class types into one ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2390](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2390)), fixed an `if`-fusion miscompilation in `js_simpl` that could collapse two evaluations of an effectful expression into one ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2393](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2393)), and merged initial **OCaml 5.6** support ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2227](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2227))
- **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)** reworked ppx hover expansion to call Merlin's `expand-ppx` command directly instead of hand-reconstructing output, fixing broken hover text for `[@@deriving ...]` on mutually recursive types ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1615](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1615), fixes [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1614](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1614)), and switched its nix sandbox's default OCaml version to 5.5 ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1616](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1616))
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)** fixed relocatable-compiler detection for OCaml >= 5.5 ([ocaml/dune#15444](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15444), fixes [ocaml/dune#15443](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15443)), aligned C compiler vendor detection with the OCaml compiler's own identifiers ([ocaml/dune#15423](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15423)), and stopped crashing when `~/.config/dune` is a regular file rather than a directory ([ocaml/dune#15475](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15475), fixes [ocaml/dune#15406](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15406))
- **[ocaml/odoc](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc)** removed dead compatibility code for OCaml versions older than 4.08 from the loader and model ([ocaml/odoc#1458](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1458))
- **[ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)** added a regression test confirming project-wide occurrences/renaming correctly resolves a module name mid-path, alongside a GitHub Actions `checkout` v6→v7 upgrade across all workflows ([ocaml/merlin#2081](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2081))
group_summaries.group_overview:

- **[ocaml/odoc](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc)**: [art-w](https://github.com/art-w) continued rendering OxCaml modes in generated docs ([ocaml/odoc#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454)), and [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) extended `include functor` support with review from [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([ocaml/odoc#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452))
- **[ocsigen/js_of_ocaml](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)**: three new PRs opened by [hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) — an experimental ESM output mode ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2402](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2402)), Web Audio/Media Capture bindings ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401)), and BroadcastChannel/SharedWorker bindings ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2400](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2400)) — plus a cluster of CI-restructuring merges ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2394](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2394), [ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2395](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2395), [ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2396](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2396))

- Mode coercion on function return values is now allowed for non-local axes (e.g. `int -> int :> int -> int @ portable`), by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6407](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6407))

- New `imprecise-kind-annotation` warning (191) flags kind annotations that differ from the inferred jkind, by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#5362](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5362))

group_summaries.brief_summary: Configurable domain/thread stack sizes, Windows filename hardening, and an ephemeron-termination fix landed in ocaml/ocaml.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: New `OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=...'` stack-size option, Windows `Sys`/`Filename` fixes, and ephemeron GC correctness fixes merged in ocaml/ocaml.
group_summaries.new_features:
- New `OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=<bytes>'` option lets programs configure the minimum **system stack size** used when spawning a `Thread` or `Domain`, useful for FFI code that needs a larger native stack; documented in `man/ocamlrun.1`, the reference manual, `Thread.create` and `Domain.spawn` ([ocaml/ocaml#14195](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14195), [ocaml/ocaml#14860](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14860)) by [@Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse), reviewed by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA)
- `Sys.file_exists`/related `Sys` primitives now use `GetFileAttributes` instead of `stat_os` on Windows, avoiding a kernel bug in `GetFileInformationByName` that made `Sys.file_exists "C:\\...\\repro:xxx"` wrongly return `true` ([ocaml/ocaml#14919](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14919), reported as [ocaml/ocaml#14911](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14911)-adjacent) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)
- `Filename` functions on Windows now treat `:` strictly as the drive/volume separator rather than sometimes as a directory separator, fixing surprising results from `Filename.concat` on paths like `C:\Foo:` ([ocaml/ocaml#14871](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14871), [ocaml/ocaml#14916](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14916)) by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)
- Fixed a hang in `caml_shutdown()` under `OCAMLRUNPARAM="c=1"` (cleanup-at-exit mode) where the final GC cycle could get stuck in `Phase_sweep_and_mark_main` because orphaned ephemerons from a terminated domain were never adopted ([ocaml/ocaml#14906](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14906)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole)
- Multicore GC now waits for **all domains** to finish marking before starting another round of ephemeron marking, avoiding unnecessary marking work at the cost of potentially longer GC cycles in some workloads ([ocaml/ocaml#14774](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14774)) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), reviewed by [Damien Doligez](https://github.com/damiendoligez)
- `Unix.EACCES` documentation typo fixed (previously misspelled `EACCESS`) in `unix.mli`/`unixLabels.mli` ([ocaml/ocaml#14920](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14920)) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- Memory-model documentation comments in `runtime/memory.c` clarified to be more precise about how GC frontiers update ([ocaml/ocaml#14857](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14857), [ocaml/ocaml#14924](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14924)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole)

weekly_summary.new_features_summary: Opam 2.5.2 (CVE-2026-57825 fix), configurable domain/thread stack sizes in ocaml/ocaml, js_of_ocaml WebGL2/5.6 support, and eio hardening shipped.
weekly_summary.new_features:
- __RUMINANT:core__ A new `OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=<bytes>'` option lets programs configure the minimum **system stack size** used when spawning a `Thread` or `Domain`, useful for FFI code needing a larger native stack, by [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse), reviewed by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA) ([ocaml/ocaml#14195](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14195), [ocaml/ocaml#14860](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14860))
- __RUMINANT:core__ `Sys.file_exists` and related primitives now use `GetFileAttributes` instead of `stat_os` on Windows, avoiding a kernel bug that made paths like `C:\...\repro:xxx` wrongly report as existing, and `Filename` functions now treat `:` strictly as the drive separator, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([ocaml/ocaml#14919](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14919), [ocaml/ocaml#14916](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14916))
- __RUMINANT:core__ Fixed a hang in `caml_shutdown()` under cleanup-at-exit mode where orphaned ephemerons from a terminated domain were never adopted by the final GC cycle, by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole) ([ocaml/ocaml#14906](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14906)), alongside a fix so the multicore GC waits for all domains to finish marking before another ephemeron-marking round, by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) ([ocaml/ocaml#14774](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14774))
- __RUMINANT:tools__ **[ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam)** released **opam 2.5.2**, fixing a symlink bypass of the switch-prefix check tracked as **CVE-2026-57825** ([ocaml/opam#7005](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7005), backported in [ocaml/opam#7006](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7006)), and switched internal repository storage to gzipped tar archives to speed up `update`/`init` on NTFS and IO-constrained machines ([ocaml/opam#6625](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6625)); the release also landed in __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ opam-repository across 8 packages by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30237](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30237), [ocaml/opam-repository#30238](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30238))
- __RUMINANT:tools__ **[ocsigen/js_of_ocaml](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)** merged **WebGL2** bindings closing a long-standing request ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2388](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2388), [ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#1226](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/1226)), fixed an `if`-fusion miscompilation in `js_simpl` that could collapse two evaluations of an effectful expression into one ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2393](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2393)), and merged initial **OCaml 5.6** support ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2227](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2227))
- __RUMINANT:tools__ **[ocaml/ocamlfind](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind)** now installs `.cmx` files alongside `.cmi` files during `make install`, resolving warning-58 reports in downstream projects such as Rocq, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([ocaml/ocamlfind#120](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/120), fixes [ocaml/ocamlfind#117](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/117))
- __RUMINANT:tools__ **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)** reworked ppx hover expansion to call Merlin's `expand-ppx` command directly, fixing broken hover text for `[@@deriving ...]` on mutually recursive types, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1615](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1615), fixes [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1614](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1614))
- __RUMINANT:multicore__ **[ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio)** added `Address_lookup_failed` errors to `Eio.Net.getaddrinfo` instead of silently returning `[]`, reworked `Eio.Path.load` to fix reads of zero-size files such as `/proc` entries, hardened `Eio.Path.chown`/`chmod` against sandbox escape via symlinks, and added `blksize`/`blocks` fields to `Eio.File.Stat.t`, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#866](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/866), [ocaml-multicore/eio#869](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/869), [ocaml-multicore/eio#877](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/877), [ocaml-multicore/eio#865](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/865))
- __RUMINANT:oxcaml__ oxcaml/oxcaml extended the reaper's unboxing transformation to boxed `int32`/`int64`/`nativeint` numbers via a new `Boxed_number` field constructor, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6437](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6437)), and now rejects functional record updates that implicitly read an `[@atomic]` field nonatomically, by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6453](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6453))
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ New **union-find-lattice** persistent union-find/lattice library based on the authors' SAS 2026 paper, by [Dorian Lesbre](https://github.com/dlesbre) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30207](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30207)), and **Caqti 3.0.0** released as a breaking API change requiring existing users to add `caqti.classic` to their link lines, by [Petter A.
